SMTO-EXE-0163 — SMTO blocked a repeat of a desktop step

GUID: 393438f3-a9d2-5668-a7f3-a918eaa39756
Slug: ui-duplicate
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO tried to send a desktop step that the Gateway had already received or cancelled. To avoid doing the same thing twice, the Gateway refused it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the app on the Gateway's computer to see whether the earlier step already happened. The Gateway already received that step once, so its change may already be there.
  2. If it already happened, tell SMTO in the conversation so it carries on from there. This keeps SMTO from trying to do the same thing again.
  3. If it didn't happen and you still want it, ask SMTO to do that step again as a new action, and approve it if SMTO asks. A new action is tracked separately, so the Gateway will accept it.

What success looks like

  • The app shows the change once, and SMTO moves on to the next step.

If it still fails

  • If SMTO keeps getting this message for new steps, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; this points to a software problem, not to anything on your computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • UIService refused dispatch because the execution_id is already active or in its retained set of finished or cancelled identities (most recent 4096).

What this means

  • The UI service found the execution ID in its active or retained finished/cancelled identity set and refused another dispatch. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • The UI service found the execution ID in its active or retained finished/cancelled identity set and refused another dispatch.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect its original receipt and current application state before considering distinct new work.

How to fix it

  • Do not reuse execution IDs. Reconcile the original operation's effect with ui.snapshot or ui.element, and issue any deliberate new action under a new operation_id/execution_id; repeated duplicates for fresh operations point to a runtime replay defect.
  • This execution ID was already used or cancelled. Reconcile current state before a deliberate new operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • This execution ID was already used or cancelled. Reconcile current state before a deliberate new operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The original action is settled and any new deliberate operation has its own authorized identity.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
